neighbours.label: a fiction scene of action and dialogue, as opposed to quotes and dialogue in news, interviews, transcripts, lessons and reviews (all items here run over several lines, so layout is not tested, and dialogue itself is present on both sides)
fire:
Rachel set the letter on the kitchen table and stepped away from it.
"Aren't you going to open it?" Ben asked.
"Not yet."
He picked up his coffee and watched her over the rim.
"You're scared," he said.
She didn't answer.
The elevator doors closed behind them, and for a moment neither of them moved.
"You could have told me," Hannah said.
"I tried."
She laughed without any humor and pressed the button again.
He reached for her arm.
"Don't."
Jack stopped at the edge of the porch and took off his hat.
"Evening, Ruth."
She kept her eyes on her sewing.
"You've got some nerve coming here."
He turned the hat in his hands and waited.
"Is she awake?" Liam whispered from the doorway.
Meg looked up from the chair beside the bed and shook her head.
"The fever broke an hour ago."
He came in quietly and sat on the floor.
She closed her eyes.
Amy pushed her plate away. Her mother was still talking about the wedding.
"You've barely eaten," her mother said.
"I'm not hungry."
Amy stared at the tablecloth and counted to ten.
"Is this about Paul?"
The captain lowered his binoculars and handed them to the girl beside him.
"Tell me what you see."
She squinted at the horizon.
"Nothing, sir."
He smiled for the first time that morning.
"Look again."
Kate found him in the garage, sitting on an overturned bucket with a beer in his hand.
"How long have you been out here?"
He shrugged.
"A while."
She leaned against the car and crossed her ankles.
"We can't stay here," Yusuf said. He was already pulling on his boots.
Leila stayed where she was, her back against the wall.
"And go where?"
He looked at her for a moment, then at the door.
She sighed and got up.

The mayor took off her glasses and looked at the crowd.
"We will rebuild," she said.
She folded the paper and stepped back.
"When?" one man asked.
He shook his head.
The council meets again on Friday.
Q: When did you start the company?
A: In 2009, with my brother.
Q: Was it hard?
A: Very. We had no money.
Q: What changed?
A: We found one big customer.
Lesson 4: At the hotel.
"Good evening. Do you have a room?" the guest asks.
"Yes, we do," the clerk says.
"How much is it?"
The clerk tells her the price.
She pays by card.
Customer: My order has not arrived.
Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. What is the order number?
Customer: It is 48213.
Agent: Thank you. It will arrive on Friday.
Customer: Thanks for your help.
The witness took the stand at ten o'clock and was sworn in.
"Where were you on the night of May 3?" the prosecutor asked.
"At work," the witness said.
The judge called a recess at noon.
The trial resumes on Monday.
Smith scored twice in the second half as United won 3-1 on Saturday.
"We worked hard," he said.
"The lads were great."
The coach praised his defence.
He said the team would rest this week.
Priya sees about thirty patients a day at the clinic in Leeds.
"Most come in with back pain," Priya said.
"Few need surgery."
She advises them to keep moving.
The clinic opens at eight.
I bought this blender in March for my daughter.
"It's so loud," she said at first.
She uses it every day now.
The lid is a little stiff.
I would buy it again.

notes: Round 2. An earlier round claimed the line break itself and failed, because a scene with no line breaks reached 0.48. Line breaks are not claimed now, and all items here have them, so this test does not separate them from genre. Earlier round's 4 non-fiction passages 0.07 or less; its 8 scenes 0.13-0.64, on line breaks, 'She', 'He'. Probes: fiction narration without dialogue 0.20-0.25, one-line lesson dialogue 0.04, Q and A 0.01, memoir 0.02, news 0.04, a fable 0.04, a romantic 2-sentence snippet 0.04. So the claim needs the dialogue scene over several lines. Peak tokens vary.
